name: Phosphenic Pathway
scope: Working sequence model for phosphene-led conscious sleep-transition exploration toward separation-related experiences. Not a universal sequence and not part of the Nova v1 ontology.

stages.label: Phosphene entry
stages.notes: Defines this pathway specifically: visual phosphene activity is used as the entry phenomenon.

stages.label: Hypnagogic structuring
stages.notes: Structured imagery and broader hypnagogic content may emerge from the initial visual field.

stages.label: Immersive scene formation
stages.notes: Optional visual branch: imagery may become spatially immersive rather than remain image-like.

stages.label: Threshold / zone de bascule
stages.notes: Operational threshold stage. Nova wording and Lux pathway interpretation remain distinct.

stages.label: Optional transition markers
stages.notes: This is a set of alternative/possibly co-occurring markers. The pathway does not require all or any particular marker.

stages.label: Non-interruption / lâcher-prise
stages.notes: Optional regulatory action represented separately from perceptual markers.

stages.label: Décrochage
stages.notes: Represents the separation-related transition in the current working model, not an ontological claim about what separates.

stages.label: Partial or complete exit-like outcome
stages.notes: Possible continuation after Décrochage. The pathway may terminate or return before this stage.

transitions.notes: Not encoded as a Nova graph law; frequency and exceptions remain to be measured.
Structured imagery may deepen into an immersive scene, but this stage can be skipped.
Working sequence hypothesis pending structured report counts.
Visual immersion is treated as one possible route into/through threshold phenomena, not a requirement.
Nova places several marker phenomena in or near the threshold; not all markers have identical source support.
Regulatory stance/action may become relevant at the threshold without being a mandatory stage.
Some markers (notably Bourdonnement intracrânien, Flottement, État vibratoire) have source support for preceding Décrochage; the entire marker set is not asserted to do so universally.

transitions.provenance: Nova v1 reviewed relation: Lâcher-prise facilitates Décrochage
transitions.notes: Operational facilitation claim; not a necessary condition and not strong causality.

transitions.provenance: Lux pathway architecture derived from Nova transition vocabulary
transitions.notes: Décrochage is modeled as passage; partial/complete exit-like states are possible outcomes rather than guaranteed destinations.

constraints: No stage order is claimed to be universal.
Optional marker stages must not be converted into prerequisites.
Temporal order does not imply causality.
Nova source terminology remains separate from Lux pathway hypotheses.
The pathway does not adjudicate metaphysical interpretations of separation or non-physical experience.
Future structured reports should be able to confirm, weaken, split, or remove any proposed transition.
